source.title: APP: Accelerated Path Patching with Task-Specific Pruning
source.authors: F. Andersen; William Rudman; Ruo-Chen Zhang; Carsten Eickhoff

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened, but the GPT-2 Small IOI entries used here are assignable.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies automated path patching to IOI in GPT-2 Small and reports circuit performance and size, directly bearing on the original circuit finding. It also compares pruning-based circuit candidates with the path-patching result.
record.gate_note: The study reports IOI circuit performance, size, overlap and qualitative head-type results. Results for other tasks and models are not included here because they do not test the specified GPT-2 Small IOI head classes and roles. The study's cited account of the original 26-head circuit is background, not a new result.
record.test_reason: The study re-derives an IOI circuit in GPT-2 small with a different procedure: automated path patching over attention heads only. It compares that circuit with a manual path-patching circuit and with vanilla FLAP pruning. These results bear on method-independence (V4) and on how much circuit performance depends on the discovery procedure (V5). The study never compares its heads with the original 26-head circuit, so V1 cannot be judged. Contrastive FLAP, Merged FLAP and APP are the authors' own methods benchmarked against their own PP ground truth, so those rows are method-performance rows.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Pruning alone yields circuits too large to be minimal; Contrastive FLAP keeps more task-specific heads. APP cuts the search space by about 56% and compute by up to 93%, with substantial overlap with PP circuits. Performance is often similar, but not on GPT-2 small IOI (82.47% vs 96.95%). The authors also note that neither PP nor APP is consistently optimal, and that PP circuits may not be unique gold standards.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the IOI task and Path Patching, but automates circuit selection with threshold criteria and also evaluates FLAP, Contrastive FLAP, and APP. The study does not reproduce the original manual head-by-head circuit analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported IOI circuit performance differs between manual and automated Path Patching and between Path Patching and APP. The study also varies Automatic Path Patching thresholds, but does not systematically test sensitivity to ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution.
record.problems: The IOI circuit evaluation uses 100 random samples, while FLAP comparisons use 200 samples; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The study focuses on circuit discovery rather than detailed circuit analysis, and does not verify all original head classes and roles. The authors also note that hyperparameter search is limited and that results may not be optimal.
record.rows_left_out: Left out results for Greater Than, Gendered Pronouns, Induction, and Docstring, and results for GPT-2 Large and Qwen models, because these do not report tests of the specified GPT-2 Small IOI circuit. Also left out computational-cost results because they do not measure the IOI circuit or its behaviour.

untested.parts: Head identities and counts against the original 26 heads and 7 classes. Class roles. Faithfulness, completeness and minimality as defined by Wang et al.
No name-mover ablation or backup-head test.
IOI circuits in GPT-2 Large and Qwen2.5 are found, but head classes and roles are not analysed or compared.
No comparison with the original circuit, no alternative ablation types, no edge-level methods such as ACDC or EAP, and a single logit-difference metric.
Ablation type, metric and prompt distribution are not varied.
Single ARENA IOI template distribution (ABB→XYZ corruption). Name orders, templates and more names are not varied.

missing.what: IOI automated PP hyperparameter sweep on GPT-2 small: sizes 13–115 heads and performance 27.37%–113.51% across K and ε, showing circuit and performance depend on threshold choice
IOI half-life of ground-truth heads under pruning (vanilla 0.92, contrastive 0.90)
Head-type composition of the automated PP IOI circuit (which Wang et al. classes appear)

record.verdict_notes: The study's ground truth is its own automated PP circuit (heads only, no MLPs), never mapped onto Wang et al.'s 26 heads. Evidence on V1 is therefore indirect and unscored. Rows for Contrastive FLAP, Merged FLAP and APP benchmark the authors' own method and were unlinked. No uncertainty is reported. PP circuits use 100 samples and FLAP uses 200.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that its circuit has the original 26 heads, enumerate the original seven classes, or test every class's stated role under patching. Its automated path-patching circuit and head-type comparison are narrower tests.
No ablation of main name-mover heads or test of backup-head self-repair is reported.
The study applies path patching to other models and tasks, but does not test whether the same IOI head classes and roles transfer across models, checkpoints, or tasks.
The study compares pruning-derived head sets with path-patching circuits, but does not test alternative ablation types or a range of evaluation metrics.

The study reports differing results for manual path patching, automated path patching, pruning, and APP, and reports circuit performance. It does not systematically vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution.
Only the study's IOI prompt setup is tested; name orders, templates, and sentences with more names are not varied.

rows.baseline: Original model average logit difference, used as the performance reference
rows.note: The paper selected the smallest circuit meeting at least 75% performance when available. This result is high performance, but does not itself verify the original head roles or faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
rows.check: The 96.95% is for a 21-head, heads-only automated PP circuit picked as the smallest with ≥75% performance. Overlap with the original 26 heads and classes is never reported, so it cannot show whether the original circuit holds. It is also a selection-dependent value. Removed from V5, since a single value shows no sensitivity.
